message.content:
The “three great schisms” in Christian history are usually identified as:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties Involved | Main Issue |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism of 1054** (also called the East–West Schism) | 1054 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | Diverging theological, liturgical, and political practices, culminating in mutual excommunications. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Various reformers (e.g., Martin Luther, John Calvin) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Critique of papal authority, indulgences, and other doctrines; led to the creation of Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, and other Protestant traditions. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of the 19th–20th centuries** (often called the “Modern Schism” or “Eastern Catholic–Orthodox Schism”) | 19th–20th CE | Eastern Catholic Churches (in communion with Rome) vs. Eastern Orthodox Churches | Issues of jurisdiction, liturgical differences, and the status of Eastern Catholic communities within the Orthodox world. |

These three events are commonly highlighted because each represents a major, lasting division that reshaped the structure, theology, and global spread of Christianity.
